Samantha —

Quick technical summary to help the call. TL;DR: we can support all three modes within your timeframe; tradeoffs below.

Hosted (fastest path)
- Timeline: onboarding + API keys and model choice in 1–3 business days
- Data residency: Hosted can be restricted to us regions (us-east-1 or us-west-2) with contractual data controls; we keep metadata in-region unless you require Private networking
- Pros: fastest, lowest setup; Cons: less isolation for audit-heavy workflows

Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Timeline: 2–3 weeks to provision dedicated GPU pool and validate performance in-scope; deterministic latency and throughput
- Cost: monthly reserved commitment (estimate in attached MAP sheet) but better predictable unit economics for high-volume workloads
- Pros: isolation, SLA-backed latency; Cons: commit required, slightly longer lead time

Private (VPC / on-prem pilot)
- Timeline: pilot ~2 weeks for networking validation; full on-prem can be 6–10 weeks depending on rack and network approvals
- Pros: maximum control/compliance; Cons: longest and most expensive to operate initially

Attached: redwood-deploy-mode-comparison.pdf with a short numerical table (latency bucket, per-token cost estimate, timeline). I also added a suggested near-term plan: start with Dedicated in us-east for predictable latency, run a concurrent 2-week Private pilot (non-PII dataset) to validate networking and legal requirements, then decide on long-term (Dedicated vs Private).

I can present the tradeoff matrix on Tue. Proposed call slots: Tue 10:00–10:30 PT or Tue 14:00–14:30 PT.

— Karthik
